rows.why: Corner cafe, open 6:00-24:00, 8 staff a shift in three shifts. Servers work the door and all carry debt; cooks work inside. Office guards and clerks pass through, so regulars and workmates tie to the keeper.

Civic office, one shift 9:30-17:30, 72 staff. Mostly clerks inside; guards at the door who start their day at the cafe and hold regular ties into it; official drivers at the bay on cash; councillors inside.
Sphere Gardens sky rail kiosk, service 5:00-1:00, one attendant per 8 h shift at the stop; regulars are riders who pass at the same hour.
Records tram kiosk, service 5:00-1:00, one attendant per 8 h shift; commuters buy at the same hour, so regulars form at the window.
Residents of the garden, pylon and rocket blocks around the civic block; the marked block makes housing a common need; many work elsewhere, some on the sheet.

notes: Fix: Office regular share raised 0.35 to 0.7, so most of its people, guards included, carry a regular tie. A tie has no position filter, so I cannot aim it at guards alone.

Question for Keel/Splice: does the expander aim a regular tie at the person's preShift unit (the café)? If not, guards' café stop won't become a tie and the keeper learns no guard's need. Needs an expander rule, not a table change.
Question for Motive: does a need entry with 'positions' leave other positions undrawn by it? I assumed yes, and listed keeper on the other entries.
Café servers draw debt (100, server only); official drivers draw cash (100, driver only). All four temperaments meet those needs.
Official-driver 8, guard 15, councillor 15, clerk 62: each gets at least one person from 72 staff.
Guards carry preShift cafe (walk and tram); clerks do not.
Starting values [S]: all weights, shares and leave-before ranges are mine, to tune by playtest.
Names: 72 given, 96 family, 12 origins, none over 9% of a pool.

hits.text:
people rules › knowledge
a person knows a fact only if they witnessed it (§05: a clear sightline within 13 m) or were told it along a tie. At the start nobody knows anything about the cell (person.memoryAtStart). The one thing a person starts knowing about others is listed in needsKnown. The cell is known by face only: a witness remembers the Fixer's face (§03), never a name.
identity in play: face; learned by: witnessed, told; the cell at the start: nothing
needs known at the start: a keeper knows the needs of workmate and unit-regular (§08 economy: café owner tips needs before Scout listens)
From DF's rumour rule (a fact exists only for those who saw it or were told) and Adams 2017 (identity stored per observer as alias, name or face). Only face is in play: the Talker's facts are a face, a car and a place-time, and §05 investigators hop by place and time, not by name. needsKnown makes §08's tip rule checkable from the cast: a keeper knows the need of each workmate and of each person with a regular tie into their unit, so a turned keeper saves the Listen (42 s) on each. How a fact spreads at runtime (told, along which ties, how fast) is Keel's rule, not this file's.

faults.fault: The guard role has regularOf café. Both guard routines stop at the café before the shift, but the requirement line reads NOT MET: 0 of 11 guards hold a regular tie into the café. So the café keeper knows no guard's need, and the Scout gets no tip on the guard. Raising the Office's regular share from 0.35 to 0.7 did not aim any guard's tie at the café.
faults.fix: Don't change the table again. Hand this to Keel/Splice (inputs: the guard routines with the café stop; done-check: a share of guards hold a regular tie into the café). The expander should aim a regular tie at the unit of the café stop. Resubmit once the requirement line reads met.
